source.title: Towards Lifecycle Unlearning Commitment Management: Measuring Sample-level Unlearning Completeness
source.authors: Cheng-Long Wang; Qi Li; Zihang Xiang; Yinzhi Cao; Di Wang

record.file_problem: None; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies sample-level machine unlearning measurement. It does not test random-label fitting, unstructured inputs, or the claim versions; its own experiments concern unlearning inference and approximate unlearning.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Arpit et al. on data memorization in related work, but reports no experiment testing the claim. Its true-label accuracy results are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The paper cites Arpit et al. in related work but reports no results on random-label fitting, corrupted-label learning dynamics, or unstructured-input fitting. Its experiments measure unlearning completeness and inference performance on ordinarily labeled data.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that IAM efficiently measures sample-level unlearning completeness using one shadow OUT model, extends to LLMs, and identifies under- and over-unlearning risks in approximate unlearning methods.
record.recipe_differences: The study develops an unlearning-inference measurement framework; it does not reproduce the original random-label experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: IAM measurement performance varies with dataset generalization, shadow data or architecture shifts, interpolation steps, and scoring parameters; these are sensitivities of the paper's unlearning-inference task, not tests of the claim.

fits_no_version.finding: The four classification benchmarks achieve approximately 100% training accuracy, with test accuracies of 72% on CIFAR-100, 86% on CINIC-10, 94% on CIFAR-10, and 95% on Purchase.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Models in these ordinary-label unlearning benchmarks fit their training data nearly perfectly while achieving dataset-dependent test accuracy.

record.problems: The paper provides no evidence on random-label fitting or the listed claim versions. The reported training accuracy is an aggregate statement without per-dataset values.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results relevant to the claim versions were reported. The paper's other tables and figures concern unlearning inference metrics or unlearning methods, not the claim's behaviors.

untested.parts: Fitting completely random labels, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Relative training time for true and random labels and convergence under increasing label corruption.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and progressive test-error degradation across label-corruption fractions.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Learning shared real-data patterns before memorizing noisy or random labels.

record.verdict_notes: Random sample removal is not random labeling. Section 5.7's negative-label condition corrupts characters in an inference-time prefix without parameter updates; it does not test learning random labels. Training checkpoints in Section 5.2 evaluate inference scores without comparing real-label and noisy-label learning order.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting, chance test error, unchanged architecture and hyperparameters, and generalization on true labels are not tested.
Training time and convergence under increasing label corruption are not tested.
Shuffled-pixel and Gaussian-noise inputs are not tested.
Training and test error across a sweep of randomized label-corruption fractions is not tested.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on random-label fitting or true-label generalization are not tested.
Learning order for real versus noisy or random labels is not tested.
